text: A weapon forged from stolen children answers only the man who built it, so the institution that commissioned it inherits a loaded gun it can never fire or destroy.
Fear of an outmatched enemy licenses each atrocity as temporary, until the leaders who authorized them find the crimes have become the foundation they now must stand on.
Whoever grants a subordinate the means to end an unstoppable enemy has also granted him the means to end his master, and the same word does both.
Survivors bury their guilt under concrete and amnestics, but the buried thing stays alive, waiting for the one voice they could not silence.
Institutions that rebuild the world after each collapse must erase their own record of having done so, and thus can never learn how often they have failed.
Resurrection at scale makes every person replaceable, and a people who can be reprinted indefinitely stop counting as losses to those who hold the printer.
Repeated fine-tuning of a species to remove its violence eventually removes the stubbornness needed to survive, so the correctors must leave the flaw in place.
A safeguard that guarantees recovery quietly licenses the recklessness it was built to survive, and each rescue spends a tolerance that cannot be measured until exhausted.
